provenance.escape: SPEC-AUTHORED. Inputs and expected values were written from html.escape's documented contract (replace & then < then >, and when quote is set " and ') without running it, then checked against CPython. A disagreement would therefore indict the port OR the spec reading, not silently inherit Python's behaviour.
provenance.composed: TRANSCRIBED from CPython output. text/verbatim/attr compose escape with educate_reader_quotes and fold_reader_characters, whose quote-direction algorithm is too intricate to author by hand. These rows therefore CANNOT detect a case where Python itself is wrong; they pin the port to the oracle only. What they do detect is the composition order and the quote flag per helper.
provenance.settable: Cases are ASCII unless marked non_ascii, because fold_reader_characters short-circuits on is_ascii and only consults the settable set beyond it.

escape.name: ampersand_first
escape.note: DISCRIMINATING: proves & is replaced before < and >. A port replacing < first yields < unchanged and passes every other row here.

escape.name: double_quote_splits_on_flag
escape.note: RULE 10c: unquoted equals the input. Paired with quoted, which differs, so the row cannot pass by never escaping.

escape.name: single_quote_splits_on_flag
escape.note: RULE 10c: unquoted equals the input; quoted differs, and pins the hex form ' rather than '.

escape.name: already_escaped_double_escapes
escape.note: escape is not idempotent; pinning this stops a port from adding an is-already-escaped guard Python does not have.

escape.name: empty
escape.note: RULE 10c: equals the input by necessity. Kept as a boundary, not as evidence.

escape.name: no_special_characters
escape.note: RULE 10c: equals the input. Kept only to pin that escape adds nothing; the discriminating rows are the ones above.
